name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.13.0 — the evidence manifest's `observed` field becomes a typed JSON object (a closed per-leg shape, unavailable numeric slots typed `{"unavailable":"<enum>"}`) instead of a packed string, and `verdict.js`'s regex-parsing (`parseCounts`/`deriveProduction`) is deleted: a string-`observed` row now derives `UNVERIFIED` instead of being silently misread, and release-ledger keys (`e2e`/`journeys`/`substrate`/`ci`) copy the leg's `observed` object verbatim instead of dropping drifted keys. A new `testCountPattern` capability lets `review-legs.js` record what a child process actually executed, and the at-risk leg now goes red the first time it hands a runner paths that execute nothing (files > 0 ∧ testsExecuted = 0), closing the 2026-08-16 vacuous-green class same-run instead of silently. This is `grounding-contract.md`'s one deliberate edit for the cycle — every host re-grounds. 7.12.0 — the pin forcing every private read of the host's `.claude/spec.config.json` through `spec/scripts/lib/host-config.js` was fail-open in two independent, executed dimensions: its predicate required the filename and a reader call (`readFileSync`/`path.join`) to appear on one line, so hoisting the filename to a constant walked straight past it, and its walk filtered to `.js`, so a three-line bash script reading the config with `jq` was never inspected at all — both probes left the suite green. The replacement stops asking the undecidable question "does this line read the config?" and asks the decidable one "does this line name the config?": any line under `spec/scripts/` containing the stem `spec.config` outside a comment is an offender, where the comment exemption is exactly `//` plus `#` not immediately followed by an identifier character — `*`, `/*`, and a trailing `//` are deliberately not treated as prose prefixes, since each begins or hides executable JavaScript. The walk now covers every file at any depth with no extension or name-shape filter, and the exemption is a closed list of exactly three literal relative paths — `lib/host-config.js`, `smoke.sh`, `spec-state-gate.sh` — rather than a pattern, since a list cannot be joined by a new file merely existing. `lib/host-config.js` gains three exports so the ban has a sanctioned route for every legitimate reason to name the file: `configPath(root)`, `configExists(root)` (a presence probe that never opens or reads the file), and `CONFIG_RELPATH`; `readConfig`, `readConfigStrict`, and `declaredForge` are unchanged. Seven remedy strings across `env-preflight.js`, `fidelity-check.js`, `review-legs.js`, and `spec-design-driver.js` now interpolate `CONFIG_RELPATH`, `fidelity-check.js`'s two messages gaining the `.claude/` prefix they were missing, and `fleet-reader.js`'s discovery probe now routes through `configExists`. Falsification is an end-to-end canary over a synthetic tree in `tmpdir()` exercising walk, predicate, and exemption together, not a fixture string fed to the predicate alone, because the failure being fixed was two components failing open independently. Accepted residual, stated honestly: a literal deliberately split across the stem itself, an encoded or computed filename, and readdir-based discovery still evade — no AST checker, since this repo is strictly zero-dependency. 7.11.0 — fleet evidence reader: a new zero-dependency script (`spec/scripts/fleet-reader.js`, `spec-paths fleet-reader`) scans every repo one level under `~/Projects` carrying `.claude/spec.config.json`, reads each in-scope repo's `.claude/spec-runs*.jsonl` ledgers (live plus year archives), and answers six fixed queries — leg red-recency, the brief-08 gate, escape aggregates, replay debt, CLEAN-contradicted-by-escape, and a schema-drift census — population-first (repos scanned, rows read, unparseable counts, oldest/newest ts always lead both renders, and a config-bearing repo with no ledger still lists at rows: 0), read-only and stateless (no writes, no cache, no stored repo list), `--json` (seven top-level keys) or a human render. Hardened at review: the machine surface writes through a looping `fs.writeSync` and no longer calls `process.exit(0)` (the old write-then-exit pair truncated `--json` at exactly 65,536 bytes when stdout is a pipe — which command substitution is — and still exited 0, i.e. a green exit carrying corrupt JSON on the very invocation the incident policy now prescribes); an unreadable ledger file or an unlistable `.claude` directory is counted in a per-repo `unreadable` bucket kept strictly separate from `unparseable` (lines read-and-rejected) and named with a remedy in both renders, so one bad file yields a partial fleet answer that says what it could not read instead of an uncaught crash or — worse — a confident `no ledger` for a repo whose ledger exists; an unreadable `--repos-root` exits 2 with a remedy rather than a stack trace; and the human render's integer percent derives from the two raw counts (`Math.round(count * 100 / total)`), since scaling a ratio by 100 in floating point rendered an exact 57.5% as 57%. Brief 17's motivating gap: pipeline questions were being answered from this repo's own ledger, ~14% of the 1,077 rows readable fleet-wide today. Two JJ-ruled doctrine changes ride along: core.md § Incident Policy's third-recurrence trigger now counts across every readable repo ledger on this machine (26 fleet-wide escapes vs at most 13 visible in any one repo) rather than one host's slice, deriving from the literal invocation `node "$(spec-paths fleet-reader)" --json`; and `/spec:escape`'s row schema gains a nullable `class` field (a stable kebab-case defect-class id, derived from evidence and confirmed in the existing classification call, `null` when underivable) so defect-class recurrence — the trigger's numerator — becomes mechanically countable going forward instead of forever hand-asserted. The reader is deliberately boring: six fixed queries, no query flags, nothing that grows toward the autopilot shape the brief names as its own failure mode.
